raw_response:
I am old now, and it is just me in the household, so I do not want to do anything too risky this year. On my 4.1 mu, I will still do wheat and then maize after it, same as before. That is the safest way here. Wheat and maize together make sure I have grain and some cash, and if one side is not so good, the other can still help. I do mostly what has worked on my land and what the neighbors around me are doing. I cannot spend too much at once, but I also do not dare use too little fertilizer because if the crop turns yellow or grows thin, the loss is bigger than the money saved.

For wheat, I will sow in October like usual, using a common improved seed from the local dealer, not anything expensive. I will put most fertilizer before sowing, then add one more topdressing around jointing if the wheat looks weak. Since we have well water, I will probably irrigate about three times for wheat if rain is not enough: once after sowing if the soil is dry, once around overwintering or revival, and once near jointing. After wheat harvest in June, I will not waste time because the maize must go in fast. I will do simple shallow tillage or just quick field cleaning and sow maize right away. For maize I will use hybrid seed like most people here. I will put some fertilizer at planting and one topdressing around knee-high stage. If summer rain is normal, maybe only one irrigation or even none, but I will plan for one because these years weather is not steady. I only spray if I see weeds or insects. Since I farm only 4.1 mu, I can still manage with my own labor, maybe hire a little machine work, but not much hand labor.
